criteria.text: Given the Command Center, when it is opened, then every tab is reachable and every card drills down one level.
criteria.evidence: Observed 2026-08-16: all 9 tabs served 200 with zero page errors; Overview carries 23 drill-down links; clicking one landed on detail.html?card=systems and rendered content.

criteria.text: Given sample mode, when any tab is shown, then the sample data is visibly labelled as sample.
criteria.evidence: Observed 2026-08-16: pressing Sample renders the banner "Sample data - believable made-up values ... Nothing here is a record of anything this project has produced." Occurrences of the word sample rise from 1 to 18.

criteria.text: Given the data files, when any tab renders, then its content comes from .colaberry/plan.json and .colaberry/progress.json read at runtime rather than from hard-coded values.
Given .colaberry/manifest.json, when any tab is shown, then it displays how old the data is and warns when that age exceeds a week.
Trust — no tab shows a number, a connection or a result the project has not actually produced.
criteria.evidence: Observed 2026-08-16: in Real mode every system reads "never checked" and every count reads 0, under the line "Grey is unknown. Nothing here turns green until something real reports in." Caveat: the hard-coded plan still says 12 stories where the current plan has 14, which is a symptom of criterion 3 being unmet.

tests_added: render harness: 9 tabs + 81 drill-downs/views, real and sample modes, 0 errors
deletion test: removing a story / agent / release / requirement / system from plan.json removes it from every tab in both modes
dangling-reference test: a fulfilled_by naming a deleted story flips its requirement to uncovered rather than reading as covered
browser test (Playwright, chromium): all 9 tabs load over HTTP with 0 console errors and the Data-as-of stamp on each
schema test: the same renderers drove both the 12-story plan and the re-synced 14-story plan with derived/schedule/due_on, unchanged
stories.notes: Criteria 3 and 4 were correctly marked FALSE by the Colaberry platform team on 2026-08-16 during a pre-cohort rehearsal: the build then made no network request for any .colaberry file and contained no reference to manifest.json, because the whole plan was hard-coded in command-center/assets/plan.js. Both are now met and that file is deleted. Criterion 3: assets/data.js fetches .colaberry/plan.json, progress.json and manifest.json at load and assets/normalise.js shapes them; no plan content is typed into any component. Verified two ways — Playwright/chromium shows all 9 tabs loading over HTTP with 0 console errors, and a deletion test shows that removing a story, agent, release, requirement or system from plan.json removes it from every tab in both modes, while adding one makes it appear. The same renderers drove both the 12-story plan and the re-synced 14-story plan (derived/schedule/due_on/fulfilled_by) without being edited. Criterion 4: App.stamp() puts 'Data as of <absolute date> (<relative age>)' in the shared shell, so it appears on all 9 tabs; CC.age() turns it amber with 'sync from the portal to refresh' past one week. Both states observed. Wording is 'Data as of', not 'last synced', because the manifest stamp moves when the data changes, not when a sync runs. Also fixed: a fulfilled_by naming a story that has left the plan no longer reads as coverage — such a requirement now reports as uncovered.

criteria.text: Given a user selects a city, when the system analyzes properties, then it displays an Opportunity Score.
Given a user selects a ZIP code, when no properties are found, then it displays a 'No opportunities' message.
Trust: The system logs the analysis process for audit.

outstanding: Given a student with valid credentials, when they log in, then they should access their dashboard.
Given a student with invalid credentials, when they attempt to log in, then they should see an error message.
Trust: All login attempts must be logged for audit purposes.

criteria.text: Given a property with a high Opportunity Score, when viewed, then it shows an AI Assessment and recommended action.
Given a property with a low Opportunity Score, when viewed, then it shows a minimal assessment.
Trust: The system logs the rationale for the recommended action.

outstanding: Given a student enrolled in a course, when the instructor views the progress, then the correct data should be displayed.
Given a student not enrolled in any course, when the instructor views the progress, then a 'no data available' message should be shown.
Trust: All data retrieval actions must be logged for audit purposes.
